newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany wants strong, large currency union - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants strong, large currency union - Dini.

text.p: Italian foreign minister Lamberto Dini said on Friday that Germany believes in a strong and large monetary union.
"Germany believes in a strong and large European currency union," Dini told reporters at the sidelines of consultations between Italian and German delegations.

Dini joined the delegation visiting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl for discussions which were likely to touch on Italy's chances for joining Europe's planned currency union at its scheduled launch in 1999.
There has been some speculation that Germany was unwilling to allow southern European nations into the currency union at the start as their consolidation efforts had not gone far enough.
Italy however has stressed that it intends to be among the first nations to join the currency union.
